instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. I need control of the keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key. But the cleaners keep locking the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I'll approve their cleaning checklist. The kettle stays out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the building manager's instructions need my approval. Otherwise accounts can't reliably have tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your deliveries keep arriving during meetings. I need to approve the van schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book the rooms. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Send the routes too. I'll approve those so the times hold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't schedule around that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give them my number. Road closures will need to fit my room bookings.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we're painting Dad's kitchen together. Since he died, I only see you when we empty a cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I pay a painter? I can't face covering his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Covering them is not approved. You may help me tape around them instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm canceling the painting. You may cry here, beside me. I miss you more than I need a clean wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've reserved ten minutes of your evening for my sculpture opening. I want you there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture. You won't need me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I decide who I need. You may ask every obvious question, just as long as you're there to ask it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I come before your mother? We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Come before we open; I'll put you in charge of helping me unpack the biggest piece. I want a memory of tonight with you in it.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kitchen passes inspection. I haven't approved your departure; we still haven't talked about whether we're okay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to wash up. The dishes are done. Can I go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The washing-up part is approved. Sit down for the part where you tell me how we got this angry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm allocating nine to us. You may leave in time for your bus, but I don't want 'the dishes are done' to be our last words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our coats are on, but I haven't approved calling the taxi. We haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologized for telling my sister about your debt. Can we go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. I need to know you won't let her inspect every choice I make at dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for it. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I authorize being late. Sit with me until I can believe you're coming as my partner, not to check that I look grateful.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your apology for missing my concert needs one more sentence before I'll accept it. What did the empty seat cost me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was canceled. Can I explain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may, after you tell me what it was like to keep looking for you. I've already heard what happened to the train.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start with the moment I looked at the door before the encore. I want you to acknowledge that I was still expecting you, not just that you weren't there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not accepting 'sorry for the silence' as the whole answer. Tell me what those six weeks did to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone broke. Doesn't that explain it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll allow it as an explanation of your phone. Now explain what it was like to keep checking mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the part I needed. Now add that I kept rewriting my message to sound easier to answer. I need you to understand what I started believing about myself.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've accepted the museum job. You may congratulate me on leaving the workshop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the move myself. I'm waiting for the man who taught me to make things to say this counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won't approve packing them for my return. Sharpen them for the museum. I need you to send me off expecting me to do well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, we've signed the lease. I've put you in charge of the toast before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The move is decided. You may tell me you're pleased, though. It still matters when it comes from you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm revising the toast to include both of us. You may take your time getting used to Sam, but tonight I want to hear my mother wish us both happiness.
